title: Whether the Government will publish a list of foreign organisations that pose national security concerns
asked: Ms Hazlina Abdul Halim asked whether the Government will publish a list of foreign organisations that may pose concerns to national security and how frequently such organisations are monitored and reviewed; what formal channels exist for Singaporeans to seek guidance before taking part in overseas activities linked to foreign organisations and whether a centralised contact point will be set up; and whether advisories or requirements will be introduced for Singaporeans intending to volunteer with foreign organisations.
response: Ms Sim Ann said the Government already publishes lists for specific national security purposes, such as foreign organisations designated as terrorist entities under the First Schedule to the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act, but there are no plans for a broader public list because it may give rise to operational and security risks. Awareness is handled through regular publicity and outreach, including the SGSecure national movement and amplification of messages through the media. Statutes such as the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act and the United Nations Act carry restrictions, travel advisories are issued where necessary, and it is ultimately each individual's responsibility to comply with the law.

key_points.point: Existing lists are published for specific national security purposes, such as terrorist entities under the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: certain foreign organisations designated as terrorist entities are listed in the First Schedule to the Terrorism (Suppression of Financing) Act

key_points.point: There are no plans to publish a broader list of foreign organisations of concern
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: There are no plans to make public a broader list of foreign organisations that may pose concerns to Singapore's national security.

key_points.point: A broader list could create operational and security risks
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: Such a list may give rise to operational and security risks.

key_points.point: Public awareness is raised through regular publicity and outreach on security threats, including foreign terrorist groups
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: Regular publicity and outreach efforts are conducted to raise public awareness of security threats

key_points.point: Singaporeans are told not to take part in foreign armed conflicts and to be careful with organisations linked to foreign militaries or security and intelligence agencies
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: Singaporeans should not participate in foreign armed conflicts

key_points.point: Statutes such as the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act impose restrictions, including on membership in a foreign legislature or foreign political organisation
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: There are also restrictions and responsibilities under various statutes such as the Foreign Interference (Countermeasures) Act

key_points.point: Travel advisories will be issued where necessary on overseas developments with security implications
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: Where necessary, the Government will issue travel advisories on overseas developments that may have security implications.

key_points.point: Individuals are responsible for complying with the law and not acting against Singapore's national interest
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: It is ultimately every individual's responsibility to ensure that they comply with our laws

key_points.point: SGSecure is the national movement used to disseminate information on security risks
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: we have a national movement to prepare Singaporeans against terrorism – SGSecure

key_points.point: Existing messages were amplified through the media in the cases raised by the Member
key_points.speaker: Ms Sim Ann
key_points.quote: we have also amplified existing messages through the media

left_open: Formal channels for Singaporeans to seek guidance before participating in overseas activities linked to foreign organisations
Whether a centralised point of contact will be established
How frequently the list and activities of such organisations would be monitored and reviewed
Advisories or requirements specifically for Singaporeans intending to volunteer with foreign organisations
How the balance would be calibrated between mitigating security risks and ensuring practical compliance
supplementary: Supplementary questions focused on awareness campaigns and partnerships with agencies, community organisations and schools to raise public awareness of security risks.
